overview: Two tiers of the four-level biosafety containment system, reflecting escalating risk of the agents handled and the precautions required.
genZNote: BSL-2: gloves and a closed door. BSL-3: gloves, a closed door, negative pressure, and a respirator.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: The containment level for agents that pose moderate hazards to personnel and the environment via percutaneous injury, ingestion, or mucous membrane exposure.
aspects.valueB: The containment level for agents that can cause serious or lethal disease via inhalation, requiring more rigorous engineering controls.

aspects.label: Agent Examples
aspects.valueA: Staphylococcus aureus, Salmonella species, hepatitis B virus.
aspects.valueB: Mycobacterium tuberculosis, SARS-CoV-2 (culture work), Coxiella burnetii.

aspects.label: Primary Transmission Risk Addressed
aspects.valueA: Percutaneous exposure, ingestion, mucous membrane contact.
aspects.valueB: Airborne/aerosol transmission, in addition to the risks covered at BSL-2.

aspects.label: Facility Requirements
aspects.valueA: Standard lab with self-closing doors and access to a biosafety cabinet for aerosol-generating procedures.
aspects.valueB: Controlled access, negative air pressure relative to the corridor, sealed windows, and dedicated ventilation exhausted outside the building.

aspects.label: PPE Requirements
aspects.valueA: Lab coat, gloves, and eye protection as needed.
aspects.valueB: Respiratory protection (e.g. N95 or higher) in addition to standard PPE, plus more stringent decontamination practices.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Moderate-risk agents, standard precautions, biosafety cabinet as needed.
aspects.valueB: Higher-risk airborne agents, negative pressure rooms, and respiratory protection required.
